Tulsa's airline base, engine shops and aerostructures plants: sorting NAS 410, SNT-TC-1A and the airline specification

Tulsa is where airline maintenance meets oil country. American Airlines describes its Tech Ops base at Tulsa International Airport as the largest commercial aircraft maintenance facility in the world. Lufthansa Technik Engine Services, the former BizJet, overhauls business-jet engines in the city, and the former Spirit AeroSystems plant in Tulsa became part of Boeing when that acquisition closed in December 2025. NORDAM builds and repairs aerostructures here as well. A few miles away, the HF Sinclair refinery, the ONEOK and Williams pipeline systems and the vessel and heat exchanger shops that ship through the Port of Catoosa run on ASME and API codes. So three personnel documents meet in this market, not two.

The airline hangar: the manual names the standard

An airline maintenance base or Part 145 repair station certifies NDT personnel to whatever its maintenance or repair station manual specifies. The FAA does not certify NDT inspectors. Its advisory circular AC 65-31B accepts ATA Specification 105, the airline industry's own document, along with NAS 410, SNT-TC-1A, ISO 9712 and others. That is why two Tulsa hangars can certify eddy current inspectors under different documents. Ask which one the manual names, and whether any customer contract adds NAS 410 for particular component work.

Engine shops and aerostructures plants: the purchase order names it

Manufacturing and component repair for airframe and engine makers is bought on purchase orders, and their quality clauses usually call for NAS 410, or EN 4179 on European work. A Responsible Level 3 designated in writing runs the program, approves outlines and examinations, and decides what earlier training and experience to credit, while Nadcap AC7114 auditors trace each certification back to its evidence. If you arrive from a refinery crew, expect the RL3 to want more formal penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends before your first examination. See how NAS 410 certification works for the RL3's role.

The refinery, pipeline and fabrication side

Refinery mechanical integrity, the Cushing tank farms, gathering and transmission lines and ASME Section VIII shop work all call for personnel certified to SNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 where a code names it, through the employer's written practice. Many Tulsa technicians hold certifications from this side and from a hangar over a career. Each one belongs to the employer that issued it and ends when that job ends.

Records to carry between a Catoosa shop and a hangar at the airport

  1. Course outlines with hours, from Spartan College's NDT diploma or any other training you complete. Spartan itself is clear that school does not certify you; an employer does.
  2. An experience log signed by your Level II or Level III supervisor, kept method by method.
  3. Examination records, each marked with the standard and revision it was taken under.
  4. A current near-vision and color record.

An SNT-TC-1A certificate goes in that file as evidence, but it cannot stand in for a NAS 410 certification. Quality managers at shops serving both airline and industrial customers should name the governing standard on every certification, keep training files to the NAS 410 level of evidence, and plan the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, as customers require. Revision 6 also adds Appendix D, a points route that lets Level 2 personnel qualify to sit the initial Level 3 examination through defined NDT activities, which may interest experienced Level 2s on a large maintenance base.

Atlantis and Tulsa

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory self-paced online, Q&A with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in Tulsa. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Tulsa hangars or plants. Credit for outside coursework under a NAS 410 program is decided by that employer's RL3, so ask first. Repair stations and suppliers can use NAS 410 audit documentation for Tulsa repair stations and suppliers, prepared for the RL3 to approve, and aviation NDT consulting for written practices and outside agency Level III services. Compare the schemes in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A; method pages include eddy current testing training and ultrasonic testing in aviation.
